events.title: Edward III crowned after his father's deposition
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Edward III was crowned at Westminster Abbey after Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer forced Edward II from the throne. His later claim to the French crown began the Hundred Years' War.
events.html: Fourteen-year-old Edward III was crowned at Westminster Abbey after Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer forced Edward II from the throne. His later claim to the French crown began the Hundred Years' War.

events.title: US Supreme Court gathers for its first session
events.description: The Supreme Court convened at the Merchants' Exchange in New York, though too few justices had arrived to begin business until the next day. It heard no cases in its first year.
events.html: The Supreme Court convened at the Merchants' Exchange in New York, though too few justices had arrived to begin business until the next day. It heard no cases in its first year.

events.title: Revolutionary France declares war on Britain and the Dutch Republic
events.description: Days after executing Louis XVI, the National Convention declared war on Britain and the Netherlands. The conflict that followed lasted, with brief pauses, until Waterloo in 1815.
events.html: Days after executing Louis XVI, the National Convention declared war on Britain and the Netherlands. The conflict that followed lasted, with brief pauses, until Waterloo in 1815.

events.title: Texas votes to secede from the Union
events.description: A Texas convention voted 166 to 8 for secession, a decision confirmed by referendum later that month. Governor Sam Houston refused to swear loyalty to the Confederacy and was removed from office.
events.html: A Texas convention voted 166 to 8 for secession, a decision confirmed by referendum later that month. Governor Sam Houston refused to swear loyalty to the Confederacy and was removed from office.

events.title: Lincoln signs the resolution for the Thirteenth Amendment
events.description: Abraham Lincoln added his signature to the congressional resolution sending the amendment to abolish slavery to the states, though presidents play no formal role in amendments. Illinois ratified it that day.
events.html: Abraham Lincoln added his signature to the congressional resolution sending the amendment to abolish slavery to the states, though presidents play no formal role in amendments. Illinois ratified it that day.

events.title: Puccini's 'La bohème' premieres in Turin
events.description: Conducted by the young Arturo Toscanini at the Teatro Regio, Puccini's opera of struggling artists in Paris received a cool critical welcome. Audiences loved it, and it became one of the most performed operas.
events.html: Conducted by the young Arturo Toscanini at the Teatro Regio, Puccini's opera of struggling artists in Paris received a cool critical welcome. Audiences loved it, and it became one of the most performed operas.

events.title: Royal Canadian Mounted Police is formed
events.description: The Royal North-West Mounted Police merged with the Dominion Police to form the RCMP, Canada's national police force. Its scarlet tunics became one of the country's best-known symbols.
events.html: The Royal North-West Mounted Police merged with the Dominion Police to form the RCMP, Canada's national police force. Its scarlet tunics became one of the country's best-known symbols.

events.title: Trygve Lie becomes the first UN Secretary-General
events.description: The General Assembly appointed Norway's foreign minister Trygve Lie as the first Secretary-General of the United Nations. He served until 1952, resigning after Soviet opposition over the Korean War.
events.html: The General Assembly appointed Norway's foreign minister Trygve Lie as the first Secretary-General of the United Nations. He served until 1952, resigning after Soviet opposition over the Korean War.

events.title: Greensboro sit-in begins at a Woolworth's lunch counter
events.description: Four Black students sat at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina, and stayed after being refused service. Sit-ins spread across the South, and Woolworth's desegregated the counter that July.
events.html: Four Black students sat at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina, and stayed after being refused service. Sit-ins spread across the South, and Woolworth's desegregated the counter that July.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia breaks up on re-entry
events.description: Columbia disintegrated over Texas minutes before landing, killing all seven astronauts. Hot gases had entered a wing damaged by foam at launch; shuttle flights were suspended for two and a half years.
